name: Indio Maiz Biological Reserve
story: Indio Maiz Biological Reserve covers about 3,180 square kilometers on the southeastern corner of Nicaragua bordering the San Juan River and Costa Rica. It is one of the largest protected lowland forest systems in Central America and is rich in biodiversity, providing a home for jaguars, Baird's tapirs, and great green macaws.
matters: It is a key component in the proposed Mesoamerican Biological Corridor and serves as an important population stronghold for endangered species like the great green macaw and the jaguar.
